question: Should OpenClaw add a broader config mode that disables tokenized dashboard/Gateway auth, HTTPS or Tailscale URL constraints, device identity, pairing, and related HTTP/Control UI auth checks for private deployments?
rationale: The requested behavior changes Gateway operator-auth and transport security boundaries and adds public config surface, so automation cannot choose the permanent policy safely.

options.title: Keep Current Boundaries
options.body: Treat token/password, trusted-proxy, verified Tailscale identity, and explicit break-glass paths as the supported surface and reject a blanket bypass.

options.title: Sponsor Narrow Dangerous Mode
options.body: Design a named private-ingress or tailnet policy with explicit warnings, audit, docs, startup checks, and tests instead of a generic urlToken switch.

options.title: Accept External-Trust Bypass
options.body: Allow self-managed deployments to disable several Gateway safeguards and rely on external network controls for operator access.

recommendation.title: Keep Current Boundaries
recommendation.body: Treat token/password, trusted-proxy, verified Tailscale identity, and explicit break-glass paths as the supported surface and reject a blanket bypass.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history on Gateway auth hardening, Tailscale auth scope, and the fixed no-auth Tailscale exposure boundary.
